title: Notification pathways & stakeholder journey mapping - proposal
content:
Purpose:
This doc proposes a stakeholder-centered approach to alert/notification pathways in the Console. Instead of only thinking in terms of channels and thresholds, we map alerts to stakeholder journeys (oncall, product owner, SRE, billing ops, customer success) and define pathway templates that determine channel, severity translation, throttling and runbook linking.

Why:
- Current alert configuration exposes low-level knobs (channel, threshold) but not a clear mapping from an incident to who needs to act and how.
- Teams repeatedly configure similar policies ad-hoc (eg. page SRE for infra lag, slack channel for degradation, email for billing) — we should capture these patterns as reusable "pathways".
- Goal: reduce noise for oncall, speed correct routing, make policy inheritance predictable, and give SRE/product a simple way to run incident simulations.

Personas and pain points (short):
- SRE oncall (primary): needs high-signal pages, short remediation steps, tool integration (PagerDuty, Opsgenie). Frustrated by noisy low-severity tokenization and by missed alerts during rollouts.
- Product owner (secondary): wants near-real-time visibility for regressions but prefers aggregated digests rather than pages.
- Billing ops (secondary): needs batched anomalies and audit trail (email + console).
- Customer success (tertiary): gets notified for high-sev customer impact, wants customer context in the alert.
- Platform admin: manages tenant-level defaults, wants predictable inheritance and easy override.

Core concepts introduced:
1) Pathway template: a named template (eg. "sre-critical-pathway", "product-digest-pathway") that encapsulates channel list, severity mapping, dedup window, throttling, auto-silence rules, and default runbook. Teams can attach templates to routes or services.

2) Stakeholder lens: pre-configured audience profiles (oncall, owner, cs, finance) used when previewing impact of a policy. Each lens highlights the subset of notifications that would reach that audience.

3) Severity translation matrix: defines how system severities map to channel severities per pathway. Eg: system=WARNING might map to slack=info, email=digest, pager=none. Introduces a "severity attenuation" concept to avoid paging on low-value events.

4) Noise score and auto-mitigation: compute simple heuristic noise_score = (alert_rate_last_1h * avg_tokens) / unique_affected_entities. Use thresholds to suggest auto-muting, aggregation, or adjusted thresholds.

5) Simulated incidents runner: lightweight simulator in Console that replays historical metric slices through a pathway and shows which stakeholders would be notified, how many pages/emails, and estimated token cost. Useful for audit and rollout validation.

Wireframe notes (high-level, left-to-right flow):
- Top bar: "Pathways" / "Policies" / "Simulate" tabs.
- Pathway list: left rail with search, tags, and toggle for global vs org-specific templates. Each row shows name, primary channels, recent triggered-rate, and last edit. Quick actions: clone, attach to service, preview.
- Pathway detail canvas (center):
  - Header: name, description, owner, status (active/draft).
  - Visual map: icons for detectors -> severity translation block -> channel lanes (pager, slack, email, console-notif) -> actions (runbook link, webhook). Use thin arrows showing dedupe windows.
  - Policy table below: per-detector threshold overrides, per-environment overrides (prod/staging), and inherited default indicator.
- Preview / Simulate pane (right): select a time range or sample incidents, pick stakeholder lens, run, and see timeline of notifications with counts and estimated cost.

Channel affinity matrix (proposal):
- PagerDuty/Opsgenie: only for system severity >= CRITICAL or user-defined critical incidents; default dedupe window 5m; include runbook link.
- Slack (team channel): severity >= WARNING but attenuated for known noisy signals; default batching window = 2m.
- Email digest: daily or immediate for billing-related signals; include audit context (runbooks + customer id).
- Console persistent notification: always available, low-noise, aggregated.
- Webhook: for downstream automation and escalations.

Threshold suggestion heuristics (quick rules):
- Use historical 95th percentile baseline for latency/slo regressions and set warning at +3x sigma for initial threshold suggestions.
- For error-rate spikes, require absolute count floor (eg. >= 5 errors in 5m) to avoid noisy pages for tiny customers.
- For embeddings/usage anomalies (cost-related), use percent-change over expected daily pattern (hour-of-day adjusted).

Policy inheritance and overrides:
- Default templates can be org-wide. Services inherit by default but can opt into a more restrictive or permissive pathway.
- Visual flagging for overridden settings with breadcrumb to parent template.
- Rollout plan: introduce templates in read-only mode for 3 weeks, then allow team opt-in, then auto-apply opt-in to new services only.

Runbook and playbook linking:
- Encourage runbook snippets in alert body via templating (variables: service, environment, last_deploy_sha, first_seen_ts, relevant-slo, runbook-url).
- Pathways should provide a "runbook hint" field (short markdown) surfaced in mobile push and pager.

Escalation rhythm & temporal rules:
- Allow per-pathway escalation policies: e.g., page on initial critical, if ack not received in 2m escalate to level-2, if not resolved in 30m notify product-owner and create console incident.
- Quiet hours support: channel-specific quiet-hours with policy fallback to pager-only for severe incidents.

Simulations and audits:
- Simulator should export a CSV summary: timestamps, pathway, channel, recipient-set, simulated-page-count.
- Scheduled audits: weekly "noise report" per pathway with false-positive signals and suggested tuning (auto-created tickets JIRA-ENG-XXXX).

Accessibility and mobile considerations:
- Compact pager format (first line: short description, 2nd line: action), include deep link to Console incident.
- Slack messages should include interactive buttons (ack, create-incident, mute-signal).

Design constraints / technical notes for engineering:
- Keep evaluation logic server-side; pathways are metadata and the runtime should resolve translation quickly.
- Use existing notification-service integrations (PagerDuty, Slack, SES) but add an orchestration layer for pathway-level dedupe.
- Initial MVP: implement pathway templates, preview, and pager+slack channels. Defer email-digest and webhook batching to phase 2.

Backlog (initial, prioritized):
- P1: API + UI for creating pathway templates (JIRA-ENG-10234) - front+back.
- P1: Pathway preview panel + stakeholder lens (JIRA-UX-2231).
- P2: Severity translation editor and default templates for common patterns (SRE, product, billing).
- P2: Simulator service + CSV export (JIRA-OPS-1109).
- P3: Quiet-hours + escalation rhythm editor.
- P3: Noise-scoring heuristics runbook suggestions.
- Nice-to-have: automated threshold suggestion job that posts a suggested diff for review.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- How do we surface third-party cost (eg. large embedding requests) in the same pathway without leaking billing details to SRE? (proposal: add "billing-context" toggle to pathway).
- Should we allow per-customer runbook overrides for multi-tenant incidents?
- Rollout guardrails: default opt-in vs opt-out for org templates — recommend opt-in for safety.

Next steps (immediate):
- Sync with SRE and Solutions Eng to collect 6 canonical pathway patterns by end of Oct. (owners: Maya, Luis)
- Design sprint for preview pane microcopy and mobile formatting (owners: Priya, Ethan).
- Spike: build a basic simulator that replays 3 months of error-rate anomalies for one service (owner: eng-platform).

Notes to reviewers: this is deliberately focused on a stakeholder-first mental model rather than new low-level knobs. The idea is to make common routing patterns easy to apply, to give teams confidence when changing routing, and to enable safe rollouts via simulation. Feedback requested: any major missing stakeholder types, missing channel constraints, or legal/compliance concerns with runbook content in notifications.
